title: FORAGE AND PASUTE ESTABLISHMENT
text:
FORAGE AND PASUTE ESTABLISHMENT

Objectives
1. Identify and familiarize the recommended forage species in dairy farming;
2. Learn the technical propagation methods of grasses and legumes;
3. Identify noxious weeds in tropical pasture;
4. Identify other application of forage.

Recommended grasses for dairy cattle:
1. Mulatto II (Brachiaria decumbens x B. ruziziensis x B. brizantha)
2. Napier (Pennisetum purpureum)
3. Corn (Zea mays)

Recommended grasses for dairy cattle:
1. Rensonii (Desmodium cinereum)
2. Madre de cacao (Gliricidia sepium)
3. Ipil-ipil (Leucaena leucocephala)

Feed Quality | Mainly old grass: Low | Mainly young grass: Medium | Young grass & legume: High
Digestibility of Feed | Mainly old grass: Low | Mainly young grass: Moderate | Young grass & legume: High
Breakdown rate in the rumen | Mainly old grass: Slow | Mainly young grass: Moderate | Young grass & legume: Fast
Daily DM feed intake as % of body weight | Mainly old grass: Less than 1.5% | Mainly young grass: 1.5%- 2.5% | Young grass & legume: 2.5%- 3.5%
Which will give..... | Mainly old grass: POOR animal production | Mainly young grass: MODERATE animal production | Young grass & legume: GOOD animal production

How to establish forages?
A. Land Preparation
1. Plowing - helps loosen the soil and eliminate weeds and most of the residues of the previous crop.

facts: The chapter or section title on Page 28 is 'FORAGE AND PASUTE ESTABLISHMENT'.

The four learning objectives are: 1. Identify and familiarize recommended forage species in dairy farming; 2. Learn technical propagation methods of grasses and legumes; 3. Identify noxious weeds in tropical pasture; 4. Identify other application of forage.
Recommended grasses for dairy cattle include Mulatto II (Brachiaria decumbens x B. ruziziensis x B. brizantha), Napier (Pennisetum purpureum), and Corn (Zea mays).

The page lists forage legumes/trees (under the heading 'Recommended grasses for dairy cattle'): Rensonii (Desmodium cinereum), Madre de cacao (Gliricidia sepium), and Ipil-ipil (Leucaena leucocephala).
Mainly old grass has low feed quality, low digestibility, slow rumen breakdown rate, daily dry matter (DM) feed intake of less than 1.5% of body weight, and results in poor animal production.

Mainly young grass has medium feed quality, moderate digestibility, moderate rumen breakdown rate, daily dry matter (DM) feed intake of 1.5% to 2.5% of body weight, and results in moderate animal production.

A combination of young grass & legume provides high feed quality, high digestibility, fast breakdown rate in the rumen, daily dry matter (DM) feed intake of 2.5% to 3.5% of body weight, and results in good animal production.
The first step of forage establishment under Land Preparation is plowing.
Plowing helps loosen the soil and eliminate weeds as well as most residues of the previous crop.
